question: In the channelized-intersection example in Figure 2A-3, how far from the nose of the island is the YIELD sign shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B (channelized intersection) of Figure 2A-3, the YIELD sign is shown at a lateral offset of 6 feet to 12 feet minimum from the nose (edge of pavement) of the channelizing island. Per the figure's note, this offset is a minimum of 6 feet measured from the edge of the shoulder, or 12 feet measured from the edge of the traveled way. (The STOP sign mounted on the island itself is shown with a separate 2-foot minimum clearance to the island edges.) Guidance (recommended): - "Any signs or signals placed on a raised island in the center of an undivided highway should be installed with a clearance of at least 2 feet from the outer edge of the raised island to the nearest edge of the sign or signal, except as permitted in Section 2A.16." (This corresponds to the 2 ft MIN. dimensions shown for the island-mounted sign in Drawing B, distinct from the YIELD sign's 6–12 ft offset.) Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-3, Drawing B ("Channelized intersection"), shows a dimension arrow labeled "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." from the island nose to the YIELD sign, with the figure note stating the lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. Citations: - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Section 8A.06 Guidance §3 (p.989)
gold_answer: At least 2 feet from the nose of the island.
